correctness.rationale: Read pinned RESULT.md and checker.py. For n=m+1 regular-simplex vertices, same-edge, adjacent-edge and disjoint-edge absolute inner products are a=2/(m+1), b=(m-3)/(m^2-1), c=4/(m^2-1); the chosen scaling gives sum vv^*=I. Unsigned vertex-edge incidence Q obeys Q^TQ=2I+A and QQ^T=(n-2)I+J, deriving triangular graph adjacency eigenvalues 2(n-2), n-4, -2 with multiplicities 1,m,N-m-1. G=(a-c)I+(b-c)A+cJ therefore has Lambda=4(m-2)/(m+1), Theta=(m-3)(m-5)/(m^2-1), Nu=8/(m^2-1). The transverse maximum switches at m=7, producing gamma=4m(m-3)/(m^2-1) for m<=7, gamma=(3m-7)/(m-1) for m>=8, and all transverse eigenvalues coincide m=7. Orthogonal splitting t=hu+z proves the deficit on the entire nonnegative unit sphere; a small strictly positive eigenvector perturbation realizes equality, and positivity of gap gives unique uniform maximizer. Independent numerical real-symmetric eigensolver recreated spectra for m=4..12, not substituted for universal proof. m=3 excluded because no positive rigidity gap.
